Carpenter/Maintenance Assistant- part time
Salary: Band 6 £19,945 - £23,467pa (FTE £33,241 - £39,219 pa)
Working Hours: 22.5 hours per week, 52 weeks
Closing Date: 6 September 2026
Can you make the difference to the lives of our students? Do you like to be challenged? Are you solution focused?
Do you want to be part of our SEMH school?
This could be the job for you.
Although West Heath School can be a challenging place to work, our dedicated staff rebuild lives through education. Teaching respect, encouraging responsibility, building relationships, and developing resilience in our students is an integral part of the role. Our committed, dynamic, and resourceful staff find working at West Heath School rewarding. We are currently on an exciting journey to be registered as a therapeutic community and welcome staff who follow this ethos.
The successful candidate would be a dual-skilled professional within the Estates and Facilities team. This specialist role provides high-level carpentry expertise alongside comprehensive general maintenance support to ensure the smooth, secure, and efficient running of the school’s physical infrastructure and daily operations.
Due to the nature of the role the ideal applicant must hold, NVQ 3/City & Guilds in Carpentry or equivalent with significant experience in construction and repair. A more general knowledge of general maintenance is also required.
As a school we are proud to promote the development of life skills and social development as equal to academic achievement. West Heath School works towards the end goal of helping students re-integrate into mainstream learning and preparation for adulthood.
Please complete and submit the Equality and Diversity Form alongside your Application Form.
Working at West Heath School involves close and unsupervised contact with vulnerable groups including children and as such is a regulated activity. The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. Applicants must be willing to undergo safeguarding screening appropriate to the post (including an Enhanced DBS check. Management positions will require a 128 Check.)

pageCache.text:
Satchel:One
Here at West Heath we make use of an online learning tool – Satchel:One (formally Show My Homework) – to help you keep track of your child’s learning. It allows you to see the details of tasks your child has been set including, where appropriate, details around task completion, due dates and grades.
Satchel:One is an invaluable tool in supporting students catch up on work that they may have missed in class, to keep up with their learning if, for whatever reason, they are unable to be in school, or perhaps to review and revise what’s been learned. It allows for effective communication between students and their teachers giving the opportunity for two-way feedback between teacher and student on completed work, or even to request some additional help.
The system also helps maintain communication between teachers and you, the parents. Parents are able to set up a personal account, using a code supplied by the School, which is linked to your child’s learning calendar. It provides all the information, tools and support to allow you to get involved and support your child’s learning. Click here for your Team Satchel Parent Welcome Pack to help you to navigate around and get the most out of the system.
To keep up to date on the move, you can download the Satchel:One app which you can use once you have your login details. You will then be sent notifications to let you know if and when home learning is due. You will also be informed of grades and any overdue tasks, as well as receiving information relating to other events or school announcements.
Satchel also produce useful Student and Parent video guides.
If you have any questions about the service, please don’t hesitate to make contact with the experts via https://contactus.satchelone.com or call 0207 1979550

Parent/Carer resources
We are thrilled to present a dedicated collection of PDF resources focusing on online safety for our parents/carers.
In this digital age, ensuring a secure online environment for our children is paramount. Especially at the rapid rate our technology is moving. Our carefully curated materials will help keep you in the loop. These are provided by The National College and cover topics such as internet etiquette, app description/awareness, age-appropriate content guidelines, and practical tips on how to adapt to a healthy digital lifestyle. These PDF's will update throughout each term as trends/app usage change throughout the academic year.

Summer Parent/Carer resources
We have pulled together information about Holiday Activities and Food Programme (HAF) provision and other holiday club routes across a number of local authority areas. HAF is usually for children and young people who receive benefits-related free school meals, although some councils may also offer referred or discretionary places.
Families should use the links below to check live availability, eligibility, booking deadlines and voucher-code instructions. Holiday club spaces can fill quickly and each council or provider manages its own bookings.
The accompanying poster gives a quick visual summary. This page gives the full link list, including other local directories for paid holiday childcare, SEND short breaks, library events and community activities.
The school is sharing these links for information only. Families remain responsible for checking whether an activity is suitable for their child, including cost, age range, SEND support, accessibility, safeguarding arrangements, transport and cancellation policies.

pageCache.text:
Exam Results and Guidance
"...improved life opportunities through supporting children to achieve qualifications as well as invaluable life skills..."
If you are a student reading this page and would like guidance on taking exams, the importance of following the rules and regulations and also dealing with exam stress, please check out this YouTube video and also follow the links on the images below:
You should also have received from the school, or should be receiving shortly, seven JCQ documents, copies of which are attached at the foot of this page, that the JCQ have recommended you read. Year 11 students should also have received the Year 11 Exam Handbook 2025-26 and we have added to the list below a Year 11 Revision Booklet. Finally, a copy of the Summer 2026 Exams Timetable has been uploaded.
For parents seeking information regarding exam results and appeals, there is a guidance document, also at the foot of the page.
We are really proud of the progress that West Heath students make, not just in their academic studies but in their personal and social development also. Our job as a school for SEMH learners is to provide improved life opportunities through supporting children to achieve qualifications as well as invaluable life skills that will prepare them for adulthood.
.Given the complex nature of our students and the broad demographic of needs and starting points for each individual, there is no value to comparing results with other schools or publishing in league tables. Each student is individual and each year group is different. We celebrate student progress and success in many ways. For example:
An anxious student increasing their attendance who has previously refused school, is progress and we celebrate it.
A student who has experienced early childhood trauma who learns to make eye contact and trust an adult to talk to, is progress and we celebrate it.
Educationally, our culture is to support students to achieve the best possible grade that they can in each subject area, taking into account their starting point, their individual needs and abilities as well as any extrinsic or pastoral situations which affect their focus, wellbeing and emotional state. We aim to stretch and challenge each student appropriately, so that they are motivated and engaged in their learning. Many of our students have been out of school for long periods of time and we work hard to bridge gaps in learning. The common starting point with this is to make school a positive experience again for students by creating a nurturing, caring and flexible approach to learning.
Most students will continue their post-16 education with us in our popular Sixth Form and then move on to either continued Further Education, employment and training or Higher Education at University. Each year, students impress us with their maturity as they embark on their transition away from the support of West Heath School towards exciting new opportunities.
This year’s exams have gone well, 27 students sitting GCSEs with 2 transferred students included, we had a total of 56 students achieve 50 qualifications that were offered. This year we also offered a new maths qualification which was equivalent to an AS level, which was passed with flying colours. We look forward to seeing some of our students in 6th form moving onto college and level 3 qualifications. All the students should be extremely proud of all their achievement as we are of them. Congratulations to you all.
